title: embeddings-rerank-incident-breadcrumbs-maya-patel-2026-03-05
content:
Purpose: supplementary breadcrumbs and quick follow-ups after the 2026-03-03 embeddings->rerank incident. This is a personal scratchpad to capture a couple more small tests and clarifications for the handoff notes I left on 2026-03-04.

Short recap (same incident):
- Window: 2026-03-03T14:12-14:45 UTC. Symptoms: 400 dimension-mismatch errors for some customers + p95 latency spikes (~1.2-1.6s) for large rerank batches.
- Root suspects: routing selecting incompatible pool (embed dim mismatch), canary quantized-512 rollout altering runtime path and increasing tail latency for large batches, mixed SDKs emitting different embedding dims.

Extra quick checks I ran 2026-03-04 evening:
- Confirmed router preserves custom embedding metadata header when traffic flows through simple LB setup: ran a small proxy that added X-Embedding-Dim: 384 and saw it arrive at rerank-service on local dev env. Suggests production LB could be stripping or rewriting headers (need infra check).

- SDK check: pulled tenant-89 sdk usage logs (internal):
  - 2026-03-03 14:04-14:09 UTC saw ~1200 requests using embed-lite-384 via mobile pool (version: sdk-1.1.8).
  - After 14:10, we started seeing router fallback to canary because default pool had high cpu. That explains intermittent failures.

- Kernel/time profiling: ran local perf with quantized-512 on batches 16/32/64/80. Observed a non-linear jump in scheduling latency at >64 likely from GPU scheduling / pinned memory pressure. Also saw an extra 120-180ms in model unpack/quant-decode path for quantized variant.

Additional error snippets I captured from logs:
- "ERROR validate_embedding_dims: expected=512 actual=384, requestId=def456 tenant=tenant-89"
- "WARN router: routing to canary due to pool saturation default-pool->canary-2026-03-02-a"

New smaller experiments to try (TODOs):
- Inject X-Embedding-Dim header in full routing path for a test tenant and observe routing behavior (requires infra help to set header at ingestion gateway).
- Run quantized-512 with smaller max_batch_size (32) for canary to see p95 change; compare processing_time logs.
- Add a quick compatibility-mode endpoint on rerank-service that will accept 384-dim embeddings and internally project/resize to 512 (only for testing) to evaluate whether downstream scoring degrades. This is only for investigation, not a long-term change.

Follow-ups already assigned / notes for handoff:
- @Aran: confirm canary deployment zones & any routing config changes around 2026-03-02 to 03. Also share LB config for header pass-through.
- @Evelyn: validate whether X-Embedding-Dim header exists in ingestion gateway and if it's forwarded. If not, propose adding it.
- @Liam: help with a small perf-run to reproduce GPU scheduling tail at >64 candidates for quantized variant.
- SDK team contact: raise compatibility advisory for tenants observed on sdk-1.1.8 (Maya to draft).

Risk/notes:
- If we try to relax dim checks server-side, we risk silent scoring errors if embeddings are truly incompatible. Better to reject early and guide SDK upgrade.
- Quantized variant performance differences appear real; may need separate kernel optimizations or lower per-batch concurrency when quantized kernels are used.

Short-term mitigations I recommend now:
- Conservative: enforce dimension header check in router; reject mismatches with explanatory error + SDK upgrade link.
- Operational: temporarily pin affected tenants to default-512 pool (or to float-512) until SDKs are upgraded.
- Telemetry: add dimension-mismatch metric and alert threshold (e.g., >0.5% errors in 5m window) per-tenant.

Appendix (links & local paths):
- Local replays: ~/replays/rerank/2026-03-03/tenant-89/ (contains raw request/response payloads)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/482 (validation message patch)
- Incident ticket: JIRA-RERANK-137
- Slack: #infra C4567 thread

If I'm offline, handoff to Aran/Evelyn/Liam with this doc + the main 2026-03-04 breadcrumbs. I'll update this after we get LB header confirmation.
